summary: Inspected the Gizmo workspace/extension/profile system without modifying any files. Mapped the protocol schema, project catalog storage on disk (.gizmo/profiles.json), server-side GizmoServerExtension contract (detect / detectRoots / profile / systemPrompt / createTools), how extensions self-register globally vs per-project, and the activateExtensions pipeline that merges defaultTools with extension tools/prompts.
decisions: Workspace-type auto-detection is implemented via each GizmoServerExtension's optional `detect` and `detectRoots` hooks, plus per-extension `profile` factories; removing auto-detection means deleting/ignoring those fields across packages and from extension-host wiring.

Extensions are globally registered (gizmo.extensions.json + per-package gizmoExtension exports from packages/svelte, /unity, /git, /activity, /skill-authoring), so 'globally installed but manually enabled per project' maps to keeping registration but gating enablement through project-level state (e.g., profiles.json / project.extensions) rather than auto-activation in activateExtensions.

Default profiles are extension-supplied factories that get materialized into .gizmo/profiles.json on add; an 'ephemeral override that reverts to canonical when equal' would need to live in memory only and be compared structurally against the extension's canonical profile before applying.

WorkspaceProfile / WorkspaceProfiles / StoredProject types in packages/protocol/src/index.ts are the canonical protocol/storage shapes; project-catalog.ts is the single writer/reader of profiles.json and is the place to intercept save semantics.

User-created profiles already coexist with extension-sourced profiles via `source: 'extension:<id>'` vs user-defined entries; preserving that distinction is required for the override-vs-canonical comparison.
